description:
Make your baked goods more delicious and nutritious by adding some Organic Spelt Flour to your recipes. This flour is stone-ground to minimize the loss of nutrients. It's naturally rich in fiber and plant protein, as well as essential minerals. Adding some whole spelt flour to your baked goods will ensure that you are getting some precious iron and zinc every mouthful.

Spelt is an ancient grain and a type of wheat. Therefore, Organic Spelt Wheat Flour isn't gluten-free. However, because of its lighter texture and lower content of gluten, this flour can be an excellent whole wheat alternative. It's safe for people who want to reduce their intake of gluten for dietary reasons.

Stone-ground organic spelt flour is similar to wheat by texture, but the grain itself is much more flavorful. It has a rich nutty and mildly-sweet flavor, without any bitterness of whole wheat.


How to Bake with Organic Spelt Flour

In essence, you can use organic white spelt flour in any recipe that requires wheat flour. It's best to replace about half of the flour in a recipe with spelt flour. It will allow you to see how it works in every recipe, and you can adjust your proportions in the future.

It's important to note that whole wheat spelt flour soaks up less liquid than wheat flour. Therefore, you'll need to cut down the number of liquid ingredients by a little bit. However, you can also add a bit more flour. It is necessary to prevent the dough from being too sticky.

Store your organic stone-ground spelt flour in an airtight container someplace cool and dark. In a pantry or a cupboard, it will last for six months. It will store in the fridge for a year so go ahead and buy Organic Spelt Flour bulk.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

bullet_point: [DELICIOUS FLOUR: Whole-Grain Barley Flour has a delightfully nutty and slightly-sweet flavor that will enhance your dishes., RICH IN NUTRIENTS: Barley is a nutritionally-rich grain, and barley flour also contains a lot of essential vitamins and minerals, including B vitamins, iron, and zinc., GREAT SOURCE OF FIBER: Barley Flour contains about three times more fiber compared to white wheat flour., EASY TO USE: You can use Finely Ground Barley Flour on its own or in flour mixes., VERSATILE FOR BAKING: As it contains a small amount of gluten, Barley Flour great for cookies, muffins, and shortbread.]
description:
You can easily make your baked goods more nutritious and delicious by adding some Barley Flour. Whole-Grain Barley Flour provides you with all the benefits of this incredible grain. It also contains some gluten. Therefore, you can use this flour on its own and not only in mixes since gluten helps the dough rise.

Food To Live Barley Flour is finely ground. It’s made from hulled barley using stone-grinding to minimize the loss of nutrients. By default, barley flour contains almost three times as much fiber as wheat flour.

Barley is also more nutritious than wheat. Therefore, this flour contains more essential minerals (iron and zinc) and B vitamins. The taste of whole-grain barley flour is also different. Whereas white wheat flour is almost tasteless, barley flour is mildly sweet and nutty. Therefore, by using it in a recipe, you enhance its taste even without any additional flavorings.


Finely Ground Barley Flour Uses and Storage Guide

Barley Flour contains some gluten, but only a little of it. Gluten is the ingredient that makes yeast rise and stretch. So this flour is best used in recipes where you don’t need the dough to rise.

For example, it’s the right choice for muffins, cookies, and flatbreads. You can also use it to make delicious and nutritious pancakes for breakfast.

If you want to add the benefits of barley to your bread or even pie crust, you can mix whole-grain barley flour with all-purpose flour.

Barley flour stores for about four months and needs to stay in a cool and dry place. Always keep it in a sealed airtight container. Double-check the seal after every use.

If you want to extend the shelf life of the flour, keep it in the freezer. But make sure that the container you use is 100% airtight. Otherwise, the flour will soak up moisture from the air.

Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description: This Organic Heritage Pastry Unifine Flour is made from soft white wheat grown on the Azure Farm in Dufur, OR and has bran reduction, highly regarded by pastry chefs. This flour with a reduced bran content, is lower in protein and higher in carbohydrates than the hard wheat varieties and is therefore better suited for light and flaky pastries, pies, cookies, muffins, cakes, pancakes, and waffles, adding a delicious earthy flavor. All natural, no preservatives or additives, no bleaching or enriching. Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

description: Neapolitan pizza dough Makes 48 ounces dough or five 9.5-ounce portions, enough for five 9-inch pizzas INGREDIENTS: 1/2 teaspoon (3 grams) fresh cake yeast 2 cups lukewarm water (90° to 100°F) 1 tablespoon table salt or fine sea salt 2 lbs/910 g Caputo flour plus more for dusting INSTRUCTIONS: In a small bowl, using a fork, stir the yeast into 1 cup of the lukewarm water. Set aside until the yeast dissolves, about 5 minutes. In another small bowl, combine the salt and remaining 1 cup water. Stir to dissolve the salt. To make the dough by hand: Place 7 1/4 cups (2 pounds) of the flour in a large bowl. Make a well in the center of the flour and stir in the yeast mixture, along with the saltwater mixture. Using a wooden spoon, mix the dough, incorporating as much of the flour as possible. Turn the dough out on a lightly floured work surface and knead until soft and elastic, 12 to 15 minutes. It will still be a little sticky but shouldn’t stick to your hands. Add only a minimum amount of flour to the work surface to keep the dough from sticking. To prepare the dough for rising: Cut the dough into fifths to form five even portions, each weighing 9.5 ounces. Pick up one portion of dough and pull the opposite edges together, wrapping them underneath towards the center to form a tight, smooth ball. Pinch to seal. Repeat with the other four portions. Place each portion in a 1-gallon lock-top plastic bag. Squeeze out all the air and seal the bag, allowing enough room for the dough to double in size. Let rise in a cool room (about 60°F) for 6 to 8 hours. Alternatively, refrigerate for at least 10 hours or up to 24 hours. Remove from the refrigerator 3 hours before using to allow the dough to come to room temperature. Proceed with any Neapolitan pizza recipe.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Wheat, the ?Staff of Life,? is the top cereal crop in the world ? followed by corn and rice. It is the staple grain for at least a third of the world?s population. Wheat is ubiquitous in the American diet - in breads, pasta, crackers, breakfast cereals, baked goods and pastries. Wheat is classified according to planting season (winter or spring), hardness of the kernel (hard or soft) and color of the kernel (red or white). Winter wheat is planted in the fall and harvested in early summer; spring wheat is planted in spring and harvested in late summer. Hard red winter and hard red spring wheat are higher in protein than soft wheat and are most commonly used for all-purpose flour and yeast breads. Durum wheat is the hardest variety, and is used to make pasta. Soft red winter and soft white spring wheat are milled into flour for making cakes, cookies, pastries and crackers. The color of wheat kernels is in the bran layer; white wheat lacks the genes for color that red varieties have. To cook one cup of hard red wheat, soak overnight, drain then add 4 cups of water, bring to a boil then simmer for 45-60 minutes. After cooking will yield 2 ½ cups. description:
Make your baked goods more delicious and nutritious by adding some Organic Spelt Flour to your recipes. This flour is stone-ground to minimize the loss of nutrients. It's naturally rich in fiber and plant protein, as well as essential minerals. Adding some whole spelt flour to your baked goods will ensure that you are getting some precious iron and zinc every mouthful.

Spelt is an ancient grain and a type of wheat. Therefore, Organic Spelt Wheat Flour isn't gluten-free. However, because of its lighter texture and lower content of gluten, this flour can be an excellent whole wheat alternative. It's safe for people who want to reduce their intake of gluten for dietary reasons.

Stone-ground organic spelt flour is similar to wheat by texture, but the grain itself is much more flavorful. It has a rich nutty and mildly-sweet flavor, without any bitterness of whole wheat.


How to Bake with Organic Spelt Flour

In essence, you can use organic white spelt flour in any recipe that requires wheat flour. It's best to replace about half of the flour in a recipe with spelt flour. It will allow you to see how it works in every recipe, and you can adjust your proportions in the future.

It's important to note that whole wheat spelt flour soaks up less liquid than wheat flour. Therefore, you'll need to cut down the number of liquid ingredients by a little bit. However, you can also add a bit more flour. It is necessary to prevent the dough from being too sticky.

Store your organic stone-ground spelt flour in an airtight container someplace cool and dark. In a pantry or a cupboard, it will last for six months. It will store in the fridge for a year so go ahead and buy Organic Spelt Flour bulk.

Facts about Buckwheat:

But first, a bit of history. The buckwheat grown in Aroostook county Maine has tiny white flowers and is known as silver hulled buckwheat. This variety is grown exclusively in the northern part of Maine and parts of Canada. The farmers grew and milled buckwheat for their own consumption and the middlings or bran were used for livestock feed. They also used the hulls to insulate their homes. 

The buckwheat plant is extremely hardy and resilient, which makes it easy to grow without the use of chemicals. The short growing season here in the St. John Valley is perfect for the 10-12 weeks required to produce the buckwheat seed. 

The word buckwheat actually comes from a Dutch word meaning beech wheat and refers to the fruit of the buckwheat, which resembles a 
tiny beech nut. Buckwheat is not a grain but an herb or fruit closely related to wild rhubarb, making buckwheat flour Gluten-Free. 

Cross contaminations is highly improbable because there is no rye, wheat, or barely grown on the farm. Our mill is used strictly to mill our own buckwheat. description: Organic Kamut Unifine Flour is milled from grain considered part of the "ancient grains" category, and more nutritious than regular wheat due to a higher protein and potassium content. It also contains a unique type of gluten that is said to be easier to digest than common wheat gluten. Kamut flour, which is yellow rather than light brown, can be used for bread, muffins and other baked goods as well as for homemade pasta. It has a rich "buttery" taste, high nutritional value and is also easy to digest. All natural, no preservatives or additives, no bleaching or enriching. Kamut is sourced from organic farms in the USA Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising.

that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite

description:
If you want to make soft and delicious pastries, you definitely should use pastry flour. White Wheat Pastry Flour from Food To Live is made by stone-grinding soft wheat. This particular type of flour has a lower gluten content because it has less protein.

By the way, Did you know that protein creates a sticky substance we call gluten when flour mixes with water?

Furthermore, gluten is the element that affects the yeast in the dough. Its chemical love affair makes the yeast rise and stretch.

All-purpose flour has a higher gluten content. Therefore, it’s the right choice for bread and other recipes where the dough needs to rise.

Wheat Pastry Flour works much better for non-rising recipes; it gives your baked goods the delightfully soft and flaky texture by default.


When to Use Soft Wheat Pastry Flour

Sifted Wheat Flour is best used for pie crusts, homemade pasta, cookies, and croissants. You can also use it to make delicious blueberry muffins and cranberry scones. The idea is to use this type of flour when you want the pastries to be soft and fluffy in texture.

Note that soft wheat flour is rather tasteless. Therefore, it’s convenient that it can be used in almost any recipe. We find it works amazingly to make the batter for fried dishes.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite

description:
Rye is a family of wheat. Whole-grain rye flour contains the highest amount of bran. Therefore it's rich in proteins, vitamins, potassium, iron, and magnesium. Rye flour is popularly used in diets for people with diabetes since the rye's carbohydrates are brake down gradually and, therefore, prevent blood glucose levels from rising quickly. Rye contains many proteins and amino acids, so even athletes can benefit from it in their diet.
How does it taste and how can you use it

Rye flour possesses a unique taste and color. The taste is slightly bitter and nutty, which is surprising for those who like wheat bread.
Another quality of rye flour is its ability to become brown when baked. That is why the crumb of rye bread is always dark.
For a long time, whole rye flour was only for industrial baking of bread. However, nowadays, it is becoming more common, and the number of recipes with rye flour continuously grows. You can make cookies, pancakes, pies, tortillas, and other goodies from it. Different mixing proportions - different properties of your bread
Because bread flour possesses different characteristics than wheat flour, it is rarely used as a substitute. Instead, bakers use it to make a flour mix. Here are some examples of bread with the use of different proportions of rye and wheat flours:
The bread that has up to 40% rye flour, commonly referred to as "rye bread." Rye flour is in a reasonably large proportion here; therefore, there is a distinct rye flavor.
Bread with more than 50% rye flour is entirely different. All the unique characteristics of rye and wheat's chemical differences become more important as the proportion of rye in the dough increases. Typically this bread is flatter and should be allowed to rest for a few hours after baking to prevent crusting.
When there is 70% rye or more, the bread may need to rest for 24 hours, even up to several days, before slicing.

bullet_point: [Wheat gluten is a food made from gluten, the main protein of wheat., It is made by washing wheat flour dough with water until all the starch granules have been removed, leaving the sticky insoluble gluten as an elastic mass, which is then cooked before being eaten., On its own, vital wheat gluten is sodium-free, fat-free, saturated fat-free and contains no cholesterol., In the form of seitan or other meat analog, it is a good protein alternative for vegetarians or anyone looking for meat substitutes.]
description:
► Vital wheat gluten provides the extra gluten that whole-grain loaves need to rise their highest. It's particularly helpful in loaves that use low-gluten or whole grain flours, such as rye, oat, teff, spelt, or buckwheat.

► Vital wheat gluten is like a super-powered flour that is all gluten and very little starch. It's not technically flour itself, but it's made from wheat flour that has been hydrated to activate the gluten and then processed to remove everything but that gluten. It's then dried and ground back into a powder.

► Sometimes seitan is also called wheat gluten because it is made from vital wheat gluten, water, and spices, but when talking about bread recipes, vital wheat gluten flour is what is used.

► The vital wheat gluten is high in protein and low in carbs. It can also give keto flours the body they need to make doughs that are close to the real thing. The vital wheat gluten could be the ingredient your recipe needs to add that texture and structure to the baked goods.

description:
Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

Great River Organic Milling se encuentra en la parte superior del río Mississippi, en el corazón de lo que se llama el Valle de Hiawatha. La belleza natural de la zona es un recordatorio constante de la importancia de nuestro compromiso con la agricultura orgánica. La agricultura orgánica o sostenible es más que la evitación de fertilizantes químicos y pesticidas. Una granja orgánica se esfuerza por proteger nuestro medio ambiente mediante la construcción y el mantenimiento de suelos saludables que, a su vez, mejora la calidad del agua y del aire. Se ha demostrado que los granos y otros cultivos alimenticios cultivados en un suelo saludable, resisten mejor a las plagas y enfermedades que los cultivos cultivados convencionalmente y también contienen nutrientes más vitales importantes para los seres humanos. El consumo de alimentos orgánicos promueve la salud de las personas y la tierra en la que se cultivó. Al apoyar la agricultura orgánica promovemos el ciclo de un ambiente saludable que incluye la vida de microorganismos, plantas y humanos. La mayor parte de la harina del Gran Río es de piedra molida. Creemos que las piedras de molino de granito natural contribuyen a la calidad, el sabor y la integridad nutricional de la harina de grano entero. El grano que fluye en las piedras se vuelve muy delgado, copos planos que integra todas las partes del trigo inmediatamente en la harina, permitiendo que la harina tenga más sabor. Las temperaturas más frías que se producen durante el fresado con piedras permiten que continúe la actividad enzimática importante. También se mantienen los niveles de proteínas. Nuestras harinas molidas de piedra se molen a pedido, para conservar el valor nutricional de la harina. Great River está certificado orgánico por Quality Assurance International y Kosher aprobado. La obtención de nuestra certificación requiere una inspección anual de nuestras instalaciones de fresado y registros para asegurar que nuestros productos cumplan con los estándares de la industria.

Great River Organic Milling befindet sich am oberen Mississippi Fluss, im Herzen des Hiawatha Valley. Die natürliche Schönheit der Gegend erinnert immer an die Bedeutung unseres Engagements für die biologische Landwirtschaft. Die biologische oder nachhaltige Landwirtschaft ist mehr als die Vermeidung von chemischen Düngemitteln und Pestiziden. Eine Bio-Farm strebt danach, unsere Umwelt zu schützen, indem sie einen gesunden Boden aufbauen und pflegen, der wiederum die Wasser- und Luftqualität verbessert. Es wurde gezeigt, dass Getreide und andere Lebensmittelpflanzen, die in einem gesunden Boden angebaut werden, Schädlingen und Krankheiten besser widerstehen als konventionell gewachsene Kulturen und auch mehr lebenswichtige Nährstoffe enthalten, die für den Menschen wichtig sind. Der Verzehr von biologischen Lebensmitteln fördert die Gesundheit der Menschen und das Land, auf dem es angebaut wurde. Zur Unterstützung der biologischen Landwirtschaft fördern wir den Kreislauf einer gesunden Umwelt, die das Leben von Mikroorganismen, Pflanzen und Menschen umfasst. Most Great River Mehl ist steingemahlen. Wir glauben, dass die natürlichen Granitmühlsteine zur Qualität, Geschmack und Nährstoffintegrität von Vollkornmehl beitragen. Getreide, das in die Steine fließt, werden sehr dünne, flache Flocken, die alle Teile des Weizens sofort in das Mehl integrieren, sodass das Mehl mehr Geschmack hat. Die kühleren Temperaturen, die beim Fräsen mit Steinen auftreten, lassen wichtige Enzymaktivität fortsetzen. Auch der Proteinspiegel wird beibehalten. Unsere steingemahlenen Mehle werden auf Bestellung gemahlen, um den Nährwert des Mehls zu erhalten. Great River ist organisch zertifiziert durch Qualitätssicherung International und koscher genehmigt. Die Erhaltung unserer Zertifizierung erfordert eine jährliche Inspektion unserer Fräsanlage und Aufzeichnungen, um sicherzustellen, dass unsere Produkte den Industriestandards entsprechen.

A Great River Organic Milling está localizada no alto rio Mississippi, no coração do que é chamado de Vale Hiawatha. A beleza natural da região é um lembrete constante da importância do nosso compromisso com a agricultura orgânica. Agricultura orgânica ou sustentável é mais do que evitar adubos químicos e pesticidas. Uma fazenda orgânica se esforça para proteger o nosso meio ambiente, construindo e mantendo solo saudável que, por sua vez, melhora a qualidade da água e do ar. Foi mostrado que grãos e outras culturas alimentares cultivadas em um solo saudável, resistem a pragas e doenças melhor do que culturas convencionais e também contêm nutrientes mais vitais importantes para os seres humanos. Consumir alimentos orgânicos promove a saúde das pessoas e a terra em que foi cultivada. Ao apoiar a agricultura orgânica, promovemos o ciclo de um ambiente saudável que inclui a vida de microrganismos, plantas e seres humanos. A farinha de Great River é moída em pedra. Acreditamos que as pedras de granito naturais contribuem para a qualidade, sabor e integridade nutricional da farinha de flor integral. O grão que flui nas pedras torna-se muito fino e plano, que integra todas as partes do trigo imediatamente à farinha, permitindo que a farinha tenha mais sabor. As temperaturas mais frias que ocorrem durante a moagem com pedras permitem que a atividade enzimática importante continue. Os níveis de proteína também são mantidos. Nossas farinhas moídas em pedra são moídas sob encomenda, para reter o valor nutricional da farinha. Great River é certificado orgânico pela Quality Assurance International e aprovado pela Kosher. Obter nossa certificação requer uma inspeção anual de nossas instalações de fresagem e registros para garantir que nossos produtos atendam aos padrões da indústria.

Great River Organic Milling 位於密西西比河上岸,位於所謂的 Hiawatha 山谷的中心。 該地區的自然美不斷地提醒我們對於有機農業承諾的重要性。 ​ 有機或可持續的農業不僅僅是避免化學肥料和殺蟲劑。 有機農場致力於通過建造和維持健康的土壤來保護環境,進而改善水和空氣質量。 已顯示,穀物和其他食物作物生長在健康的土壤中,比傳統種植的作物更好抵抗害蟲和疾病,也含有更多對人類重要的營養素。 食用有機食物可促進個人健康,促進其生長的土地。 ​ 支持有機農業,我們促進健康環境的循環,包括微生物、植物和人類的生活。 ​ 大多數 Great River 麵粉都是石地。 我們相信天然花崗岩磨石有助於全穀物麵粉的品質、味道和營養完整性。 流入石頭的穀物變得非常薄,扁平的薄片,可立即將小麥的所有部分整合到麵粉中,讓麵粉有更多的味道。 在用石頭研磨過程中出現的更涼溫度,使重要的酶活性得以繼續。 ​ 蛋白質水平也保持不變。 我們的石粉是按訂單研磨的,以保留麵粉的營養價值。 ​ Great River 通過 Quality Assurance International 有機認證,並獲得猶太認證。 要獲得我們的認證,必須對我們的銑削設施和記錄進行年度檢查,以確保我們的產品符合行業標準。

Great River 有机研磨位于密西西比河上部,所谓的海华达山谷中心。 该地区的自然美不断提醒着我们对有机农业的承诺的重要性。 有机或可持续的农业不仅仅是避免化学肥料和农药。 一个有机农场努力通过建造和维护健康的土壤来保护我们的环境,从而提高水和空气质量。 研究表明,谷物和其他食品作物在健康的土壤中生长,抵抗害虫和疾病,比常规种植的作物更好,而且含有对人体重要的营养素。 有机食物可促进个人和其生长地的健康。 为了支持有机农业,我们促进包括微生物、植物和人类的生命在内的健康环境循环。 大部分 Great River 面粉是石粉的。 我们相信天然花岗岩磨石有助于全谷物面粉的质量、味道和营养完整性。 谷物流入石头变得非常薄,扁平的薄片将小麦的所有部分都整合到面粉中,让面粉具有更多的味道。 在石头研磨过程中发生的较冷温度使重要的酶活性得以继续。 蛋白质水平也维持。 我们的石粉按订单打磨,以保持面粉的营养价值。 Great River 经过国际质量保证和犹太洁食认证。 要获得我们的认证,需要每年检查我们的铣削设备和记录,以确保我们的产品符合行业标准。

그레이트 리버 오가닉 밀링은 히와타 계곡이라고 불리는 중심의 미시시피 강 위 부분에 위치해 있습니다. 이 지역의 자연적인 아름다움은 유기농 농업에 대한 우리의 헌신의 중요성을 지속적으로 상기시키는 것입니다. 유기농, 지속 가능한 농업은 화학 비료 및 살충제를 피하는 것 이상입니다. 유기농 농장은 건강한 토양을 만들고 유지함으로써 환경을 보호하기 위해 노력하며, 이는 차례로 물과 공기 품질을 향상시킵니다. 건강한 토양에서 자란 곡물 및 기타 식작물은 전통적인 재배 작물보다 해충과 질병에 저항하고 인간에게 중요한 더 중요한 영양소가 포함되어 있다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다. 유기농 음식을 섭취하면 개개인과 그것이 자란 땅의 건강을 촉진합니다. 유기농 농업을 지원하기 위해 미생물, 식물 및 인간의 삶을 포함한 건강한 환경의 사이클을 촉진합니다. 가장 그레이트 리버 밀가루는 돌로 갈아 입습니다. 저희는 천연 화강암 밀스톤이 통곡물 가루의 품질, 맛 및 영양 무결성에 기여한다고 믿습니다. 곡물이 돌에 흐르는 매우 얇고 평평한 플레이크로 밀의 모든 부분을 밀가루에 즉시 통합하여 밀가루가 더 맛있게 만듭니다. 스톤으로 밀링하는 동안 발생하는 시원한 온도는 중요한 효소 활동을 계속할 수 있도록 합니다. 단백질 수준도 유지됩니다. 밀가루의 영양 가치를 유지하기 위해 밀가루를 순서대로 가공합니다. Great River는 품질 보증 인터내셔널 유기농 인증을 받았으며 코셔 승인을 받았습니다. 인증을 획득하려면 제품이 업계 표준을 충족하는지 확인하기 위해 매년 밀링 시설과 기록을 검사해야 합니다.

description:
A Traditional Central American Corn Flour

Make your own tamales and tortillas at home! It’s fun and easy with authentic corn masa harina, a flavorful stone ground cornmeal that’s been precooked with limewater to make the dough pliable. Masa is also wonderful in recipes that call for cornmeal.

Masa harina is a traditional Central American corn flour dried and treated by soaking and cooking the mature (hard) grain in a diluted solution of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or wood ash, a process termed nixtamalization. Soaking the corn loosens the hulls away from the kernels and softens the corn, while making it easier to digest and absorb the nutrients.

This process produces hominy, which is stone ground into masa. It is an excellent source of fiber; corn flour contains about 7.3 grams of fiber per 100 grams serving and helps to reduce constipation. It keeps you fuller longer for weight loss benefits.

It is the time-honored Central American and Mexican breakfast staple and is used in tortillas, corn chips, taco shells, tamales, and other traditional Mexican cuisine. It is the best way to elevate recipes for tacos, tamales, empanadas, and scores of authentic Mexican dishes. Make your family’s traditional recipes or create your own delicious dishes!



Una harina de maíz tradicional centroamericana

Haz tus propios tamales y tortillas en casa! Es divertido y fácil con la auténtica harina de masa de maíz, una sabrosa harina de maíz molida de piedra que ha sido precocinada con agua de cal para hacer que la masa sea flexible. Masa también es maravilloso en recetas que requieren harina de maíz.

Masa harina es una harina de maíz tradicional centroamericana seca y tratada remojando y cocinando el grano maduro (duro) en una solución diluida de cal apagada (hidróxido de calcio) o ceniza de madera, un proceso denominado nixtamalización. Remojar el maíz afloja los cascos lejos de los granos y suaviza el maíz, mientras que facilita la digestión y absorción de los nutrientes.

Este proceso produce hominio, que es piedra molida en masa. Es una excelente fuente de fibra; la harina de maíz contiene aproximadamente 0.26 oz de fibra por cada 3.53 oz de porción y ayuda a reducir el estreñimiento. Te mantiene más lleno más tiempo para los beneficios de pérdida de peso.

Es el clásico básico para el desayuno centroamericano y mexicano y se utiliza en tortillas, chips de maíz, conchas de taco, tamales y otras cocinas mexicanas tradicionales. Es la mejor manera de elevar recetas de tacos, tamales, empanadas y decenas de auténticos platos mexicanos. Haga las recetas tradicionales de su familia o cree sus propios platos deliciosos!



Ein traditionelles mittelamerikanisches Maismehl

Machen Sie Ihre eigenen Tamales und Tortillas zu Hause! Es macht Spaß und ist einfach mit authentischem Maismasa Harina, einem aromatischen Steingemahlenen Maismehl, das mit Kalkwasser vorgekocht wurde, um den Teig biegsam zu machen. Masa ist auch wunderbar in Rezepten, die Maismehl verlangen.

Masa Harina ist ein traditionelles mittelamerikanisches Maismehl, das durch Einweichen und Garen des reifen (hart) Getreide in einer verdünnten Lösung von gesaktem Kalk (Calciumhydroxid) oder Holzasche getrocknet und behandelt wird, ein Verfahren, das Nixtamalisierung bezeichnet wird. Das Einweichen des Mais löst die Schalen von den Kernen weg und macht den Mais weicher, während es die Nährstoffe leichter verdauen und aufnehmen lässt.

Dieser Prozess erzeugt wohnliche Steine, die zu Masa gemahlen sind. Es ist eine ausgezeichnete Faserquelle, Maismehl enthält etwa 7,3 Gramm Ballaststoffe pro 100 Gramm Portion und hilft, Verstopfung zu reduzieren. Es hält Sie länger voller für Gewichtsverlust.

Es ist das altehrwürdige zentralamerikanische und mexikanische Frühstück und wird in Tortillas, Maischips, Taco-Muscheln, Tamales und anderen traditionellen mexikanischen Gerichten verwendet. Es ist der beste Weg, um Rezepte für Tacos, Tamale, Empanadas und Noten von authentischen mexikanischen Gerichten zu verbessern. Machen Sie die traditionellen Rezepte Ihrer Familie oder kreieren Sie Ihre eigenen köstlichen Gerichte.



קמח תירס מסורתי במרכז אמריקאי

دقيق الذرة التقليدي من أمريكا الوسطى

اصنع التاميل والتورتيلا الخاصة بك في المنزل! إنها ممتعة وسهلة مع ماسا هارينا الأصلية ، وهي وجبة ذرة لذيذة من الحجر الصخري تم حفظها بالماء الليمي لجعل العجين مرنًا. كما أنها رائعة في الوصفات التي تتطلب تناول الذرة

ماسا-هارينا هو طحين الذرة التقليدي في أمريكا الوسطى المجفف والمعالج عن طريق نقع وطهي الحبوب الناضجة (الصلبة) في محلول مخفف من الليمون المملح (هيدروكسيد الكالسيوم) أو رماد الخشب، وهي عملية تسمى نيكتامليزيز. نقع الذرة يخلصك من الهياكل بعيدًا عن البذور وينعم الذرة، مع تسهيل هضم وامتصاص العناصر الغذائية.

تنتج هذه العملية محلية، وهي أرضية حجري في الماسا. إنه مصدر ممتاز للألياف، يحتوي دقيق الذرة على حوالي 7.3 جرام من الألياف لكل 100 جرام للحصة ويساعد على تقليل الإمساك. يبقيك أكثر امتلاءً لفترة أطول من أجل فوائد فقدان الوزن.

إنه عنصر أساسي للإفطار في أمريكا الوسطى والمكسيكية منذ فترة طويلة ويستخدم في التورتيلا، رقائق الذرة، قشور التاكو، التامالي، وغيرها من المأكولات المكسيكية التقليدية. إنها أفضل طريقة لرفع وصفات التاكو والتامال والإمبانادا وعشرات الأطباق المكسيكية الأصلية. اصنعي وصفات عائلتك التقليدية أو اصنعي أطباق لذيذة خاصة بك!



Uma farinha de milho tradicional da América Central

Faça seus próprios tamales e tortillas em casa! É divertido e fácil com a autêntica manteiga de milho harina, uma saborosa farinha de milho moída que foi pré-cozida com água de limão para tornar a massa flexível. Masa também é maravilhosa em receitas que pedem farinha de milho.

Masa harina é uma farinha de milho tradicional da América Central seca e tratada por molho e cozinhar o grão maduro (duro) em uma solução diluída de cal (hidróxido de cálcio) ou cinza de madeira, um processo chamado nixtamalização. Deixar o milho de molho solta os cascos dos grãos e suaviza o milho, facilitando a digestão e absorção dos nutrientes.

Este processo produz o hominy, que é pedra moída em masa. É uma excelente fonte de fibra; a farinha de milho contém cerca de 7,3 gramas de fibra por 100 gramas e ajuda a reduzir a constipação. Ele mantém você mais cheio por mais tempo para benefícios de perda de peso.

É a peça básica de café da manhã mexicana e centro-americana, e é usada em tortilas, lascas de milho, cascas de taco, tamales e outras culinárias mexicanas tradicionais. É a melhor maneira de elevar receitas de tacos, tamales, empanadas e pontuações de autênticos pratos mexicanos. Faça receitas tradicionais da sua família ou crie seus próprios pratos deliciosos!

전통적인 중앙 아메리카 옥수수 가루.

집에서 나만의 타말레와 토르티야를 만들어보세요. 정통 옥수수 마사 하리나로 재미있고 쉽습니다. 석수로 미리 조리된 맛의 스톤 그라운드 옥수수 가루로 반죽을 유연하게 만들 수 있습니다. Masa는 옥수수 가루를 요구하는 레시피에서도 훌륭합니다.

Masa harina는 전통 중앙 아메리카 옥수수 가루로 성숙한(단단한) 곡물을 희석한 용액(수산화 칼슘) 또는 nixtamalization이라고 불리는 처리합니다. 옥수수를 담그면 알맹이에서 선체를 느슨하게 하고 옥수수를 부드럽게 만들면서 영양소를 쉽게 소화하고 흡수할 수 있습니다.

이 과정은 마사에 돌을 갈아 만든 소미함을 생산합니다. 섬유질의 훌륭한 공급원입니다. 옥수수 가루는 100g 당 약 7.3g의 섬유질을 함유하고 있으며 변비를 줄이는 데 도움이 됩니다. 체중 감량 혜택을 위해 더 풍성하게 오래 지속됩니다.

오랜 시간 영광의 중앙 아메리카 및 멕시코 아침 식사 필수품이며 토르티야, 옥수수 칩, 타코 껍질, 타말레 및 기타 전통적인 멕시코 요리에 사용됩니다. 타코, 타말레, 엠파나다 및 정통 멕시코 요리의 레시피를 향상시키는 가장 좋은 방법입니다. 가족의 전통적인 레시피를 만들거나 나만의 맛있는 요리를 만들어보세요!

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.

How to prepare Cachapas

– 1 cup P.A.N. Sweet Corn Mix
– 1 ¼ cups water
– ¼ cup milk
– 1 teaspoon vegetable oil
– Shortening or vegetable oil to grease the pan

PREPARATION

1. Pour water, milk and oil into a bowl. Slowly add P.A.N. Sweet Corn Mix and stir until homogeneous. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
2. Pour a portion of the batter with a ladle on a greased hot pan or griddle and spread it to make 5-6 inch wide discs.
3. Cook for 3 minutes on each side until golden brown.
4. Side with butter and fresh white cheese, or any other filling of your choice.

Ingredients include pre-cooked yellow corn meal, powdered cellulose, cane sugar, corn bran, salt, soy lecithin, riboflavin and folic acid. It may contain

description: Bulgur for human consumption is usually sold parboiled, dried and partially de-branned. Bulgur is a whole grain. Bulgur is sometimes confused with cracked wheat, which is crushed wheat grain that has not been parboiled. Whole-grain, high-fiber bulgur and cracked wheat can be found in natural food stores, Middle Eastern specialty grocers, and some traditional grocery stores. Bulgur is a common ingredient in Turkish, Middle Eastern, Indian and Mediterranean dishes. It has a light, nutty flavor. In the United States bulgur is produced in four distinct grinds or sizes (#1 Fine, #2 Medium, #3 Coarse and #4 Extra Coarse grinds.) It can be found in both conventional and organic forms. Bulgur can be used in pilafs, soups, bakery goods, or as stuffing. In breads it adds a whole grain component. It is also a main ingredient in tabbouleh salad and kibbeh. Its high nutritional value makes it a good substitute for rice or couscous. In Indian cuisine, bulgur or daliya is also used as a cereal with milk and sugar. In Turkey, it is prepared as pilaf in chicken stock, with or without sauteed noodles, or cooked with tomatoes, onions and red pepper. A variety of mezes and main dishes are also prepared with bulgur such as çig köfte, içli köfte, kisir and ezogelin soup. In Cyprus it is used to make koupes (also known as bulgur koftesi), a variety of kibbeh. It also forms the base of a soup, tarhana, which is made with yogurt to which hellim/halloumi has been added.

description:
A Traditional Central American Corn Flour

 

Make your own tamales and tortillas at home! It’s fun and easy with authentic corn masa harina, a flavorful stone ground cornmeal that’s been precooked with limewater to make the dough pliable. Masa is also wonderful in recipes that call for cornmeal. 

Masa harina is a traditional Central American corn flour dried and treated by soaking and cooking the mature (hard) grain in a diluted solution of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or wood ash, a process termed nixtamalization. Soaking the corn loosens the hulls away from the kernels and softens the corn, while making it easier to digest and absorb the nutrients.

This process produces hominy, which is stone ground into masa. It is an excellent source of fiber, corn flour contains about 7.3 grams of fiber per 100 grams serving and helps to reduce constipation. It keeps you fuller longer for weight loss benefits.

It is the time-honored Central American and Mexican breakfast staple and is used in tortillas, corn chips, taco shells, tamales, and other traditional Mexican cuisine. It is the best way to elevate recipes for tacos, tamales, empanadas, and scores of authentic Mexican dishes. Make your family’s traditional recipes or create your own delicious  dishes!

description: This ancient grain Einkorn Unifine Flour starts with quality organic grain from Washington State, resulting in a nutty flavor for your favorite baked goods. In this is a whole-grain product, the germ, bran, and endosperm are left intact. All natural, no preservatives or additives, no bleaching or enriching. Einkorn is sourced from organic farms in the USA. Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

1. Pour water, milk and oil into a bowl. Slowly add P.A.N. Sweet Corn Mix and stir until homogeneous. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
2. Pour a portion of the batter with a ladle on a greased hot pan or griddle and spread it to make 5-6 inch wide discs.
3. Cook for 3 minutes on each side until golden brown.
4. Side with butter and fresh white cheese, or any other filling of your choice.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

description:
Eragrostis tef is a self pollinated tetraploid annual cereal grass. Teff is a C4 plant, which allows it to more efficiently fix carbon in drought and high temperatures, and is an intermediate between a tropical and temperate grass.
The name teff is thought to originate from the Amharic word teffa, which means “lost”. This probably refers to its tiny seeds, which have a diameter smaller than 1 mm.
Teff is a fine-stemmed, tufted grass with large crowns and many tillers. Its roots are shallow, but develop a massive fibrous rooting system. The plant height varies depending on the cultivation variety and the environmental conditions.
As for many ancient crops, teff is quite adaptive and can grow in various environmental conditions; particularly, teff can be cultivated in dry environments, but also under wet conditions on marginal soils.
Teff originated in the Horn of Africa, corresponding to what is today modern day Ethiopia and Eritrea, where it is one of the most important cereals. It is grown for its tiny seeds and also for its straw to feed the cattle.
The seeds are very small, about a millimeter in length, and a thousand grains weigh approximately 0.3 grams. They can have a color from a white to a deep reddish brown. Teff is similar to millet and quinoa in cooking, but the seed is much smaller and cooks faster, thus using less fuel.

description:

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite

description:
HATTON HILL ORGANIC POLENTA (GLUTEN FREE)

One of the many Italian staple foods that have conquered the world, polenta is coarsely ground cornmeal typically used as a flavoursome base or an accompaniment for a wide range of other foods.

Its name derives from Latin, which gives you some idea of its long history. Corn – naturally, gluten-free, and from which it is milled – is believed to have been the most important food crop throughout the ancient Americas.

PURE & PREMIUM PRODUCT:

Hatton Hill Organic’s polenta is grown in the Italian sunshine, where it is dried and milled to seal in its fresh, summery flavour.

USES:

Polenta is a superb substitute for potatoes or pasta and is typically simmered like porridge to cook – often in broth or herby stock preparations to impart additional flavour. From thereon out, it is up to you how to use this versatile ingredient!

At its simplest, it forms a creamy, tasty and nutritious base for meat, fish, poultry and vegetable dishes such as ragouts and stews, but it can also be left to cool and dry, enabling it to be sliced like bread and – if you want to give it a nice finishing touch – baked, grilled, or pan-fried.

And it does not stop there! Polenta can be used like flour in baking, and like breadcrumbs to coat chicken or fish. Or how about in place of porridge or cereal for a smooth and satisfying breakfast, topped with yoghurt or fruit?

Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. description:
Ancient Grains Whole Grain Spelt Flour
Our farming industry and the American consumer has overlooked Spelt wheat (dinkel) for decades. As a result, we have not seen the same attempts to modify or enhance commercial viability of this grain. The degree of gluten in Spelt has not changed in response to overwhelming demand.


St. Hildegard Spelt Flour
Today, the composition of farro grain and spelt grains remain consistent with their ancient form during Hildegard of Bingen's time. Like einkorn flour, Hildegard Spelt flour offers moderate gluten exposure.


Organic Spelt Wheat
Modern harvesting techniques have resolved many of the challenges related to threshing Spelt, which naturally has a tough outer shell or hull. A tough hull leaves the Spelt berry naturally better protected to grow naturally.


Ancient Grains Spelt Flour
A substantial hull protects spelt grains to grow safely. The strong hull also means the grain remains fresh and retains its nutrients longer after harvest.


Spelt Flour for Baking
Try making organic spelt bread, spelt sourdough bread, vegan spelt flour cookies, ancient grain bread pudding, roasted spelt flour, spelt tortillas, spelt flour pancakes.

It can be ground into flour, or try cooked hulled spelt as a substitute for rice or potatoes, or add to soups and salads. Spelt is an ancient and distant cousin of common wheat. It is popular in Europe, especially in Germany, where it is known as dinkel, found in a variety of foods, and in Italy, where it is used in gourmet soups, pizza crusts, breads and cakes. More recently it has gained popularity in the United States due to increasing demand for higher fiber pasta and cereals. Spelt is very similar to wheat but has a slightly nuttier and sweeter flavor and it is higher in protein, fiber and B vitamins than wheat. It also has higher water solubility, so it? is more easily digested. Some people with wheat allergies are able to better tolerate spelt, but it does contain gluten so is not suitable for anyone on a gluten-free diet. Spelt has a much tougher husk than wheat, and unlike wheat, which loses its hull when harvested; spelt kernels must be mechanically hulled. It is thought that this impervious hull has its advantages, however, in that it protects the kernel from insects and pollutants, and safeguards it nutrients and freshness. To cook one cup of hulled spelt, soak overnight, drain then add 4 cups of water, bring to a boil then simmer for 45-60 minutes. After cooking will yield 3 cups. description: Organic Kamut Unifine Flour is milled from grain considered part of the "ancient grains" category, and more nutritious than regular wheat due to a higher protein and potassium content. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

title: MASIENDA Chef-Grade Masa Harina, 35.2 OZ
bullet_point: [Chef-Grade, Nixtamalized, Non-GMO/Premium Heirloom Masienda Corn, Plant-Based, Gluten-Free, Artisanal]
description: Why “Chef-Grade”? Since launching in 2014, Masienda has collaborated with chefs to develop custom, in-house masa programs for their restaurants around the world. While these programs have helped spark a fresh masa movement in professional kitchens, we recognized early on that not all kitchens would have the physical space or resources to execute daily masa production. Masa flour (masa harina) was a convenient alternative, but the leading options left more to be desired, from sourcing to quality. Masienda Chef-Grade Masa Flour was developed to solve this problem, crafted to deliver: Superior Flavor--derived from Masienda’s single-origin supply chain and culinary (never industrial) approach to sourcing Consistency--We individually dial in the cook, nixtamal and grinding processes for each scratch-made batch Ease of Use--Just add water (no molino required) How It’s Made Masienda’s Chef-Grade Masa Flour begins with single-origin heirloom corn (white olotillo) sourced from the tropical (coastal) climes of Oaxaca, Mexico. This whole-kernel corn is gently cooked and steeped in slaked lime (alkaline) water, an ancient technique known as nixtamalization. This process softens the corn, imparts calcium and activates the essential amino acids and vitamin B3 found naturally in each kernel. The kernels (now nixtamal) are then ground into a fine masa, or dough. For Masienda Chef-Grade Masa Flour, the masa then undergoes a low-and-slow drying process, which makes for a finished, shelf-stable masa flour that carefully preserves the flavor and nutrients of a freshly-milled masa. With the simple addition of warm water*, the masa is transformed into the foundation for hundreds of dishes, including corn tortillas, tamales, tostadas and other delicious preparations.

By the way, Did you know that protein creates a sticky substance we call gluten when flour mixes with water?

Furthermore, gluten is the element that affects the yeast in the dough. Its chemical love affair makes the yeast rise and stretch.

All-purpose flour has a higher gluten content. Therefore, it’s the right choice for bread and other recipes where the dough needs to rise.

Wheat Pastry Flour works much better for non-rising recipes; it gives your baked goods the delightfully soft and flaky texture by default.


When to Use Soft Wheat Pastry Flour

description: Coconut flour, made from dried, ground coconut meat, is no longer only found on the back shelves of your local health-food store. Due to its numerous health benefits, light coconut flavor and airy texture, coconut flour is making its way into mainstream stores and recipes. Use coconut flour in baked goods for a lower-carb, high-fiber and gluten-free alternative to wheat flour. Gluten- and Wheat-Free Coconut flour is a gluten-free alternative to wheat flour. Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley and rye — making traditional breads and baked goods off-limits for people sensitive to the stuff. Coconut flour enables you to bake some of your favorite cookies, pancakes and cakes without the serious side effects that may come from ingesting wheat. Coconut flour does act differently in batters than traditional grain flours, though, so you’ll need to seek out recipes that adjust the other recipe ingredients accordingly. High in Fiber With 5 grams of fiber per tablespoon, coconut flour has far more of this indigestible carbohydrate than whole-grain flour, which has just 0.8 gram per tablespoons, or white flour, which has about 2 grams per tablespoon. Much of this fiber is the insoluble type, which adds bulk to your stool, helps you feel full, deters constipation and enhances colon health. Add coconut flour to baked goods, sauces or smoothies to help you reach the recommended 25 to 38 grams of fiber daily. Higher Protein and Healthy Fats Coconut flour also contains a significant amount of protein, especially when compared to wheat flour. A 100-gram serving of coconut flour has 19 grams of protein while wheat flour has just 10. Although this protein doesn’t contain all the essential amino acids, it does contribute to your total daily protein intake to help with cell repair and growth. Coconut flour also contains about 9 grams of healthy fats per 100 grams.

description:
Make your baked goods more delicious and nutritious by adding some Organic Spelt Flour to your recipes. This flour is stone-ground to minimize the loss of nutrients. It's naturally rich in fiber and plant protein, as well as essential minerals. Adding some whole spelt flour to your baked goods will ensure that you are getting some precious iron and zinc every mouthful.

Spelt is an ancient grain and a type of wheat. Therefore, Organic Spelt Wheat Flour isn't gluten-free. However, because of its lighter texture and lower content of gluten, this flour can be an excellent whole wheat alternative. It's safe for people who want to reduce their intake of gluten for dietary reasons.

Stone-ground organic spelt flour is similar to wheat by texture, but the grain itself is much more flavorful. It has a rich nutty and mildly-sweet flavor, without any bitterness of whole wheat.


How to Bake with Organic Spelt Flour

In essence, you can use organic white spelt flour in any recipe that requires wheat flour. It's best to replace about half of the flour in a recipe with spelt flour. It will allow you to see how it works in every recipe, and you can adjust your proportions in the future.

It's important to note that whole wheat spelt flour soaks up less liquid than wheat flour. Therefore, you'll need to cut down the number of liquid ingredients by a little bit. However, you can also add a bit more flour. It is necessary to prevent the dough from being too sticky.

Store your organic stone-ground spelt flour in an airtight container someplace cool and dark. In a pantry or a cupboard, it will last for six months. It will store in the fridge for a year so go ahead and buy Organic Spelt Flour bulk.

description:
You can easily make your baked goods more nutritious and delicious by adding some Barley Flour. Whole-Grain Barley Flour provides you with all the benefits of this incredible grain. It also contains some gluten. Therefore, you can use this flour on its own and not only in mixes since gluten helps the dough rise.

Food To Live Barley Flour is finely ground. It’s made from hulled barley using stone-grinding to minimize the loss of nutrients. By default, barley flour contains almost three times as much fiber as wheat flour.

Barley is also more nutritious than wheat. Therefore, this flour contains more essential minerals (iron and zinc) and B vitamins. The taste of whole-grain barley flour is also different. Whereas white wheat flour is almost tasteless, barley flour is mildly sweet and nutty. Therefore, by using it in a recipe, you enhance its taste even without any additional flavorings.


Finely Ground Barley Flour Uses and Storage Guide

Barley Flour contains some gluten, but only a little of it. Gluten is the ingredient that makes yeast rise and stretch. So this flour is best used in recipes where you don’t need the dough to rise.

For example, it’s the right choice for muffins, cookies, and flatbreads. You can also use it to make delicious and nutritious pancakes for breakfast.

If you want to add the benefits of barley to your bread or even pie crust, you can mix whole-grain barley flour with all-purpose flour.

Barley flour stores for about four months and needs to stay in a cool and dry place. Always keep it in a sealed airtight container. Double-check the seal after every use.

If you want to extend the shelf life of the flour, keep it in the freezer. But make sure that the container you use is 100% airtight. Otherwise, the flour will soak up moisture from the air.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

bullet_point: [Made from 100% Natural Arrowroot, Batch Tested and Verified Gluten-Free, Packaged in a Bulk 5lb. Resealable Bag, Thickening Agent Used in Baking, Sauces and Gravies, Packed in California]
description:
The lack of gluten in Arrowroot Flour (powder) makes it a perfect replacement for wheat and corn based flours. Due to it's pure starch nature, Arrowroot thickens at a lower temperature than cornstarch or conventional flour. This causes Arrowroot Flour to have a more neutral taste and very smooth consistency.

Our Arrowroot is derived from the rhizomes of the Maranta Arundinacea plant, found in Thailand. The Arrowroot itself is picked, washed, and cleaned of its undesirable scales. The roots are then reduced to a pulp using large mortars, and then dried, allowing the insoluble liquids of the root to evaporate. What's left is our pure unadulterated Anthony's Arrowroot Powder.

Wait, what's that you say? You don't have any cooking needs for our Arrowroot Powder? Well perhaps you have recently been struck by a poisonous arrow and are seeking to treat your wound. Of course you are, and no doubt you've come to the right place. As the old saying goes, "When you get hit by a poisonous arrow, goto Amazon and search for Anthony's Arrowroot Powder". I know, my mother used to say it all the time as well. It has been suggested that the name "Arrowroot" was derived by a practice of ancient Caribbean tribes that used the liquid of the root as a dressing on poison-arrow wounds, as it draws out the poison when applied to the site of the injury.

However, as common as poisonous arrow wounds have become these days, we would definitely recommend using Anthony's Arrowroot Powder primarily for baking purposes, and not so much for poisonous arrow wound purposes.

Each batch of Arrowroot Powder is tested and Batch Tested and Verified Gluten-Free.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

description:
A Traditional Central American Corn Flour

 

Make your own tamales and tortillas at home! It’s fun and easy with authentic corn masa harina, a flavorful stone ground cornmeal that’s been precooked with limewater to make the dough pliable. Masa is also wonderful in recipes that call for cornmeal. 

Masa harina is a traditional Central American corn flour dried and treated by soaking and cooking the mature (hard) grain in a diluted solution of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or wood ash, a process termed nixtamalization. Soaking the corn loosens the hulls away from the kernels and softens the corn, while making it easier to digest and absorb the nutrients.

This process produces hominy, which is stone ground into masa. It is an excellent source of fiber; corn flour contains about 7.3 grams of fiber per 100 grams serving and helps to reduce constipation. It keeps you fuller longer for weight loss benefits.

It is the time-honored Central American and Mexican breakfast staple and is used in tortillas, corn chips, taco shells, tamales, and other traditional Mexican cuisine. It is the best way to elevate recipes for tacos, tamales, empanadas, and scores of authentic Mexican dishes. Make your family’s traditional recipes or create your own delicious  dishes!

– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

description: Hard Red Whole Wheat Flour is typically known as traditional "whole wheat" flour which results in outstanding baking characteristics. Azure Market's Hard Red Whole Wheat Unifine Flour is uniquely milled resulting in a fine flour, with high protein levels (about 14%). All natural, no preservatives or additives, no bleaching or enriching. Wheat is sourced from organic farms in the USA. Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description:
