dishes such as arepas, empanadas, cornbread, bollos, hallacas, pupusas, tamales to mention just a few.

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite

How to Prepare Arepas

or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. description:
Delicious arepas can now be your specialty! Harina P.A.N. is one of the most popular brands of corn flour. Versatile and perfect for a wide range of
dishes such as arepas, empanadas, cornbread, bollos, hallacas, pupusas, tamales to mention just a few.

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

make your own tamales and tortillas at home! It’s fun and easy with authentic corn masa haring, a flavorful stone ground cornmeal that’s been precooked with limewater to make the dough pliable. Masa is also wonderful in recipes that call for cornmeal.

masa Farina is a traditional Central American corn flour dried and treated by soaking and cooking the mature (hard) grain in a diluted solution of slaked lime (calcium Hydroxide) or wood ash, a process termed nixtamalization. Soaking the corn loosens the hulls away from the kernels and softens the corn, while making it easier to digest and absorb the nutrients.
Una harina de maíz tradicional centroamericana

hacer sus propios tamales y tortillas en casa! Es divertido y fácil con auténtico haring de masa de maíz, una sabrosa harina de maíz molida de piedra que ha sido precocinada con agua de cal para hacer que la masa sea flexible. Masa también es maravilloso en recetas que requieren harina de maíz.

masa Farina es una harina de maíz tradicional centroamericana seca y tratada remojando y cocinando el grano maduro (duro) en una solución diluida de cal apagada (hidróxido de calcio) o ceniza de madera, un proceso denominado nixtamalización. Remojar el maíz afloja los cascos lejos de los granos y suaviza el maíz, mientras que facilita la digestión y absorción de los nutrientes.

קמח תירס מרכזי אמריקאי מסורתי

הכינו טמלות וטורטיות משלכם בבית! זה כיף וקל עם כריכת מסה תירס אותנטית, קמח תירס טחון בטעם אבן שהיה מבושל מראש עם מי ליים כדי להפוך את הבצק לגמיש. Masa נהדרת גם במתכונים שקוראים לקמח תירס.

masa Farina הוא קמח תירס מסורתי במרכז אמריקאי מיובש ומטופל על ידי השרייה ובישול הגרגרים הבוגרים (קשים) בתמיסה מדוללת של סיד (סידן הידרוקסיד) או אפר עץ, תהליך המכונה ניקסטמליזציה. השריית התירס משחררת את הקליפות הרחק מן הגרעינים ומרככת את התירס, תוך הקלה על עיכול וספיגת החומרים המזינים

Ein traditionelles mittelamerikanisches Maismehl

Machen Sie Ihre eigenen Tamales und Tortillas zu Hause! Es macht Spaß und ist einfach mit authentischem Maismasa-Haring, einem aromatischen Steingemahlenen Maismehl, das mit Kalkwasser vorgekocht wurde, um den Teig biegsam zu machen. Masa ist auch wunderbar in Rezepten, die Maismehl verlangen.

Masa Farina ist ein traditionelles mittelamerikanisches Maismehl, das durch Einweichen und Garen des reifen (hart) Getreide in einer verdünnten Lösung aus gesaktem Kalk (Calciumhydroxid) oder Holzasche getrocknet und behandelt wird, ein Verfahren als Nixtamalisierung. Das Einweichen des Mais löst die Schalen von den Kernen weg und macht den Mais weicher, während es die Nährstoffe leichter verdauen und aufnehmen lässt.

دقيق الذرة التقليدي في أمريكا الوسطى

اصنع التاميل والتورتيلا الخاصة بك في المنزل! إنها ممتعة وسهلة مع قشور ماسا الأصلية ، وجبة ذرة لذيذة من الحجر الصخري تم حفظها مسبقًا بماء الليمون لجعل العجين مرنًا. كما أنها رائعة في الوصفات التي تتطلب تناول الذرة

الماسا فارينا هو دقيق ذرة أمريكي وسطى تقليدي مجفف ومعالج عن طريق نقع وطهي الحبوب الناضجة (الصلبة) في محلول مخفف من الليمون المملح (هيدروكسيد الكالسيوم) أو رماد الخشب، وهي عملية تسمى نيكستامليز. نقع الذرة يخلصك من الهياكل بعيدًا عن البذور وينعم الذرة، مع تسهيل هضم وامتصاص العناصر الغذائية.

Uma farinha de milho tradicional da América Central

Faça seus próprios tamales e tortillas em casa! É divertido e fácil com a autêntica colagem de masa de milho, uma saborosa farinha de milho moída que foi pré-cozida com água de limão para tornar a massa flexível. Masa também é maravilhosa em receitas que pedem farinha de milho.

Masa Farina é uma farinha de milho tradicional da América Central seca e tratada por molho e cozinhar o grão maduro (duro) em uma solução diluída de cal (hidróxido de cálcio) ou cinza de madeira, um processo chamado nixtamalização. Deixar o milho de molho solta os cascos dos grãos e suaviza o milho, facilitando a digestão e absorção dos nutrientes

传统的中美洲玉米粉

Masa Farina 是一种传统的中美洲玉米粉,通过浸泡和烹饪成熟(硬)谷物在盐酸(氢氧化钙)或木灰的稀释溶液中浸泡和处理成熟(硬)谷物,这是一种称为尼氏化工艺的过程。 浸泡玉米,让壳远离玉米粒,软化玉米,同时更容易消化和吸收营养。

中美洲傳統玉米粉

在家裡製作自己的乳酪和玉米餅! 正宗玉米片瑪莎哈拉非常有趣,簡單。這是一種美味的石頭玉米粉,預製了輕水,使麵團柔韌。 Masa 在需要玉米粉的食譜中也很棒。

masa Farina 是一種傳統中美洲玉米粉,經過乾燥處理,以稀釋的石灰 (氫氧化鈣) 或木灰浸泡和烹飪熟成 (硬) 穀物,這種工藝被稱為 nixtamalization。 浸泡玉米可使船體遠離內核並軟化玉米,同時更容易消化和吸收營養。 ​

전통적인 중앙 아메리카 옥수수 가루.

집에서 나만의 타말레와 토르티야를 만들어보세요. 정통 옥수수 마사 해링(corn masa haring)은 반죽을 유연하게 만들기 위해 석수로 미리 조리된 맛의 돌 그라운드 옥수수 가루로 재미있고 쉽습니다. Masa는 옥수수 가루를 요구하는 레시피에서도 훌륭합니다.

masa Farina는 전통적인 중앙 아메리카 옥수수 가루로 성숙한(단단한) 곡물을 희석한 용액(수산화 칼슘) 또는 nixtamalization이라고 하는 공정으로 희석된 용액에 담그고 요리합니다. 옥수수를 담그면 알맹이에서 선체를 느슨하게 하고 옥수수를 부드럽게 만들면서 영양소를 쉽게 소화하고 흡수할 수 있습니다

description:
Bud’s makes the best cricket powders available! Our crickets are produced sustainably in Thailand by farmers with decades of experience. We work hand-in-hand with the farmers to ensure that the product meets international hygiene standards, and all products are lab tested for quality.
 

What can I use cricket powder for?

For every 1 cup of flour required in a recipe, replace with 1/8 to 1/4 cup of cricket powder for added protein and nutrition. Can also be used in any other recipe or foods such as protein shakes, pancakes, pasta, mac & cheese, bread, cake, cookies, etc.

 

What does it taste like?

Our cricket protein powder has a mild taste, slightly nutty and earthy. When mixing or baking, usually the taste is unnoticeable.

 

Are crickets healthy?

Yes, crickets are actually considered a superfood. Not only do they have 2x more protein and 60% less fat than beef, they have more iron than spinach, more calcium than milk, as much vitamin B12 as salmon, and contain 17 amino acids including Lysine.

 

What is the shelf life?

Store in a cool dark place, standard shelf life is usually 12-24 months after purchase. Every bag will have an expiration date on it.

 

Are crickets good for the environment?

Crickets are one of the most sustainable and environmentally friendly protein sources on the planet. Production of traditional protein sources like beef, chicken, pork, and even soybeans are a major contributor to climate change and use massive amounts of water.

- Crickets use 100x less land than cows (per pound)

- Crickets produce 1% of the CO2 emissions of cows

Preparing the dough is an easy process:

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm

description:
Delicious arepas can now be your specialty! Harina P.A.N. is one of the most popular brands of corn flour. Versatile and perfect for a wide range of
dishes such as arepas, empanadas, cornbread, bollos, hallacas, pupusas, tamales to mention just a few.

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

description: Grain Place Foods Organic Kosher Hard White Winter Wheat whole grain wheat kernels are minimally processed. Use hard white winter wheat as you would other whole grains ? grind into flour, or cook for use in casseroles, pilaf, breakfast porridge, soups and stews, and added to breads. Wheat, the ?Staff of Life,? is the top cereal crop in the world ? followed by corn and rice. It is the staple grain for at least a third of the world?s population. Wheat is ubiquitous in the American diet - in breads, pasta, crackers, breakfast cereals, baked goods and pastries. Unfortunately, most of these products are made from refined flour, which is missing the most nutritious parts of the wheat kernel ? the germ and bran. ?Enriching? refined flour only adds a fraction of the nutrients that have been removed. Wheat is classified according to planting season (winter or spring), hardness of the kernel (hard or soft) and color of the kernel (red or white). Winter wheat is planted in the fall and harvested in early summer; spring wheat is planted in spring and harvested in late summer. Hard red winter and hard red spring wheat are higher in protein than soft wheat and are most commonly used for all-purpose flour and yeast breads. Durum wheat is the hardest variety, and is used to make pasta. Soft red winter and soft white spring wheat are milled into flour for making cakes, cookies, pastries and crackers. The color of wheat kernels is in the bran layer; white wheat lacks the genes for color that red varieties have. To cook one cup of hard white wheat, soak overnight, drain then add 4 cups of water, bring to a boil then simmer for 45-60 minutes. After cooking will yield 2 ½ cups.

description:
Rye is a family of wheat. Whole-grain rye flour contains the highest amount of bran. Therefore it's rich in proteins, vitamins, potassium, iron, and magnesium. Rye flour is popularly used in diets for people with diabetes since the rye's carbohydrates are brake down gradually and, therefore, prevent blood glucose levels from rising quickly. Rye contains many proteins and amino acids, so even athletes can benefit from it in their diet.
How does it taste and how can you use it

Rye flour possesses a unique taste and color. The taste is slightly bitter and nutty, which is surprising for those who like wheat bread.
Another quality of rye flour is its ability to become brown when baked. That is why the crumb of rye bread is always dark.
For a long time, whole rye flour was only for industrial baking of bread. However, nowadays, it is becoming more common, and the number of recipes with rye flour continuously grows. You can make cookies, pancakes, pies, tortillas, and other goodies from it. Different mixing proportions - different properties of your bread
Because bread flour possesses different characteristics than wheat flour, it is rarely used as a substitute. Instead, bakers use it to make a flour mix. Here are some examples of bread with the use of different proportions of rye and wheat flours:
The bread that has up to 40% rye flour, commonly referred to as "rye bread." Rye flour is in a reasonably large proportion here; therefore, there is a distinct rye flavor.
Bread with more than 50% rye flour is entirely different. All the unique characteristics of rye and wheat's chemical differences become more important as the proportion of rye in the dough increases. Typically this bread is flatter and should be allowed to rest for a few hours after baking to prevent crusting.
When there is 70% rye or more, the bread may need to rest for 24 hours, even up to several days, before slicing.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The lack of gluten in Arrowroot Flour (powder) makes it a perfect replacement for wheat and corn based flours. Due to it's pure starch nature, Arrowroot thickens at a lower temperature than cornstarch or conventional flour. This causes Arrowroot Flour to have a more neutral taste and very smooth consistency.

Our Arrowroot is derived from the rhizomes of the Maranta Arundinacea plant, found in Thailand. The Arrowroot itself is picked, washed, and cleaned of its undesirable scales. The roots are then reduced to a pulp using large mortars, and then dried, allowing the insoluble liquids of the root to evaporate. What's left is our pure unadulterated Anthony's Arrowroot Powder.

Wait, what's that you say? You don't have any cooking needs for our Arrowroot Powder? Well perhaps you have recently been struck by a poisonous arrow and are seeking to treat your wound. Of course you are, and no doubt you've come to the right place. As the old saying goes, "When you get hit by a poisonous arrow, goto Amazon and search for Anthony's Arrowroot Powder". I know, my mother used to say it all the time as well. It has been suggested that the name "Arrowroot" was derived by a practice of ancient Caribbean tribes that used the liquid of the root as a dressing on poison-arrow wounds, as it draws out the poison when applied to the site of the injury.

However, as common as poisonous arrow wounds have become these days, we would definitely recommend using Anthony's Arrowroot Powder primarily for baking purposes, and not so much for poisonous arrow wound purposes.

Each batch of Arrowroot Powder is tested and Batch Tested and Verified Gluten-Free.

description:
How to make delicious Seitan with our Vital Wheat Gluten Powder

Ingredients:

  • 1 teaspoon canola oil
  • 1 large white onion - chopped
  • 2 garlic clove - chopped
  • 1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds
  • 1/2 teaspoon fennel seeds
  • 1/2 cup cooked chickpeas
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1/3 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon thyme
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1/2 cup sparkling water
  • 1 1/2 cup vital wheat gluten 

Directions:

  1. Heat a large pan with canola oil. Sautée the onion and garlic cloves until they are soft. Add the cumin and fennel seeds. Cook until browned. 
  2. Add the chickpeas, onion-garlic-spices mixture, tomato paste, salt, thyme, smoked paprika, soy sauce, and sparkling water to a food processor. 
  3. After it is saucy add the vital wheat gluten and process until it becomes a ball. 
  4. Prepare a large pot with a few inches of water. 
  5. Use a steaming basket and turn the heat on high. 
  6. This is when you can mold the seitan into your meat. 
  7. Steam for about 40 minutes flipping halfway

The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

description: This ancient grain Einkorn Unifine Flour starts with quality organic grain from Washington State, resulting in a nutty flavor for your favorite baked goods. Einkorn is sourced from organic farms in the USA. Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

Food To Live Barley Flour is finely ground. It’s made from hulled barley using stone-grinding to minimize the loss of nutrients. By default, barley flour contains almost three times as much fiber as wheat flour.

Barley is also more nutritious than wheat. Therefore, this flour contains more essential minerals (iron and zinc) and B vitamins. The taste of whole-grain barley flour is also different. Finely Ground Barley Flour Uses and Storage Guide

Barley Flour contains some gluten, but only a little of it. Gluten is the ingredient that makes yeast rise and stretch. So this flour is best used in recipes where you don’t need the dough to rise.

For example, it’s the right choice for muffins, cookies, and flatbreads. You can also use it to make delicious and nutritious pancakes for breakfast.

If you want to add the benefits of barley to your bread or even pie crust, you can mix whole-grain barley flour with all-purpose flour.

Barley flour stores for about four months and needs to stay in a cool and dry place. Always keep it in a sealed airtight container. Double-check the seal after every use.

If you want to extend the shelf life of the flour, keep it in the freezer. But make sure that the container you use is 100% airtight. Otherwise, the flour will soak up moisture from the air.

Spelt is an ancient and distant cousin of common wheat. It is popular in Europe, especially in Germany, where it is known as ?dinkel,? found in a variety of foods, and in Italy, where it is used in gourmet soups, pizza crusts, breads and cakes. More recently it has gained popularity in the United States due to increasing demand for higher fiber pasta and cereals. Spelt is very similar to wheat but has a slightly nuttier and sweeter flavor ? and it is higher in protein, fiber and B vitamins than wheat. It also has higher water solubility, so is more easily digested. Some people with wheat allergies are able to better tolerate spelt, but it does contain gluten so is not suitable for anyone on a gluten-free diet. Spelt has a much tougher husk than wheat, and unlike wheat, which loses its hull when harvested; spelt kernels must be mechanically hulled. It is thought that this impervious hull has its advantages, however, in that it protects the kernel from insects and pollutants, and safeguards it nutrients and freshness. description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler milling occurring with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels will also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality assurance International and Kosher approved. This requires a yearly inspection of our records and milling facility to determine that the products labeled as organic are organically grown, processed and handled in accordance with applicable standards.

description:

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description: Hard Red Whole Wheat Flour is typically known as traditional "whole wheat" flour which results in outstanding baking characteristics. Azure Market's Hard Red Whole Wheat Unifine Flour is uniquely milled resulting in a fine flour, with high protein levels (about 14%). All natural, no preservatives or additives, no bleaching or enriching. Wheat is sourced from organic farms in the USA. Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Ultimately, Unifine milled flours from Azure are packed with many times the nutritional value compared with commercially milled flours. It has almost four times as much dietary fiber, more than twice as much potassium, and three times the magnesium. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description:
Rye is a family of wheat. Whole-grain rye flour contains the highest amount of bran. Therefore it's rich in proteins, vitamins, potassium, iron, and magnesium. Rye flour is popularly used in diets for people with diabetes since the rye's carbohydrates are brake down gradually and, therefore, prevent blood glucose levels from rising quickly. Rye contains many proteins and amino acids, so even athletes can benefit from it in their diet.
How does it taste and how can you use it

Rye flour possesses a unique taste and color. The taste is slightly bitter and nutty, which is surprising for those who like wheat bread.
Another quality of rye flour is its ability to become brown when baked. That is why the crumb of rye bread is always dark.
For a long time, whole rye flour was only for industrial baking of bread. However, nowadays, it is becoming more common, and the number of recipes with rye flour continuously grows. You can make cookies, pancakes, pies, tortillas, and other goodies from it. Different mixing proportions - different properties of your bread
Because bread flour possesses different characteristics than wheat flour, it is rarely used as a substitute. Instead, bakers use it to make a flour mix. Here are some examples of bread with the use of different proportions of rye and wheat flours:
The bread that has up to 40% rye flour, commonly referred to as "rye bread." Rye flour is in a reasonably large proportion here; therefore, there is a distinct rye flavor.
Bread with more than 50% rye flour is entirely different. All the unique characteristics of rye and wheat's chemical differences become more important as the proportion of rye in the dough increases. Typically this bread is flatter and should be allowed to rest for a few hours after baking to prevent crusting.
When there is 70% rye or more, the bread may need to rest for 24 hours, even up to several days, before slicing.

description:
Enjoy baking even more with the help of Organic Millet Flour. It will add more flavor and texture to your bread, muffins, and cookies. It’s naturally gluten-free and can be a great addition to various flour mixes.

Stone-ground hulled millet makes Organic Millet Flour, and it means that this flour retains a lot of the precious nutrients. Millet is rich in calcium, iron, and B vitamins by nature. It’s also high in protein and fiber.

People suffering from thyroid issues might want to consider and consult a family doctor before consuming millet daily. There is always a way to include it in your meal plan safely.


How to Bake with Organic Millet Flour

You can add millet flour to any gluten-free flour mix. Play around with ratios to test how it works for your recipes. Millet flour adds texture to dough and works well with sorghum flour, in particular.

Millet has a mildly-nutty and buttery flavor, which is enhanced by heating. Therefore, it will add a pleasant taste to all your baked goods.

If you don’t require flour to be gluten-free, you can mix millet with regular all-purpose flour, though be prepared to make some adjustments to the recipe as this product coarser and has more of a meal-type texture.

When using with all-purpose flour, replace ½ cup of it in the recipe with millet flour. It will result in the volume of the final baked product going down by 15% to 20%, so don’t be alarmed, the texture of the product itself will be crumbly and lovely.

Note that you also shouldn’t use more than 20% of millet flour in flour mixes for muffins, it might give your treats a slightly starchy taste.

You can also sprinkle millet flour on bread and buns before baking to make a more delicious golden crust.

Stone-ground organic spelt flour is similar to wheat by texture, but the grain itself is much more flavorful. It has a rich nutty and mildly-sweet flavor, without any bitterness of whole wheat.


How to Bake with Organic Spelt Flour

In essence, you can use organic white spelt flour in any recipe that requires wheat flour. It's best to replace about half of the flour in a recipe with spelt flour. It will allow you to see how it works in every recipe, and you can adjust your proportions in the future.

It's important to note that whole wheat spelt flour soaks up less liquid than wheat flour. Therefore, you'll need to cut down the number of liquid ingredients by a little bit. However, you can also add a bit more flour. It is necessary to prevent the dough from being too sticky.

Store your organic stone-ground spelt flour in an airtight container someplace cool and dark. In a pantry or a cupboard, it will last for six months. It will store in the fridge for a year so go ahead and buy Organic Spelt Flour bulk.

description:
Organic Cassava Flour 453.17g (16 oz.) 

Organic Cassava flour is made fromthe roots of the cassava also called yuca and manioc in other American cultures. Traditionally, the cassava is grated and placed in a press bag (woven with thatch leaves) and placed in an outdoor press where heavy stones are loaded on. Once completely drained, but still a bit moist, the cassava is beaten in a mortar then sieved to a fine flour texture. Cassava flour is not being mistaken withtapioca flour. 

Both types of flours are made fromcassava, but tapioca flour is made from cassava starch while cassava flour is made from the cassava root. Cassava is often used as a substitute for wheat flour, especially to make breads, cakes, pasta and dumplings. It is also used to make starchy custards and puddings. 

The flour is high in calories. 100 grams of cassava flour provide about 340 calories and is slightly higher than the amount that wheat flour provides (333 calories). The flour is quite low in fat, with about 1.6 gram per 100 grams. It is rich in carbohydrates (80g/100g) and in fiber (12g/100g). Cassava flour is known to attract fewer insects and pests than normal wheat flour. Cassava flour's starchy texture makes it an excellent thickener, and it is used to thicken soups, baby foods, puddings, sauces and gravies.

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

bullet_point: [GLUTEN-FREE WHEAT FLOUR SUBSTITUTE: Organic Cassava Flour is a fantastic substitute for wheat flour and contains no gluten whatsoever., REPLACEMENT FOR ALL-PURPOSE FLOUR: When baking with cassava flour, you will get the same kind of fluffy baked goods as you would with white wheat flour., FINE POWDER TEXTURE: Organic cassava flour isn’t gritty or chunky like the majority of other gluten-free flours., DELICIOUS NUTTY FLAVOR: Cassava flour has a very mild but pleasant nutty flavor that can enhance the taste of your baked goods., FULL OF FIBER: Organic cassava flour goes through minimal processing, so it retains many of the root’s natural nutrients, including fiber.]
description: With Organic Cassava Flour you can enjoy delicious cakes, buns, and other goodies with soft and fluffy texture even if you are gluten-intolerant. This is the closest gluten-free substitute for wheat flour that won’t alter the texture of your baked goods in any significant way. Also, it will enrich those treats with fiber and some trace amounts of essential vitamins and minerals. Organic Cassava Flour also has a delicious, if mild, nutty flavor. This adds another dimension to your baking making it easier for you to create true masterpieces that are 100% gluten-free. It’s made from dried and pulverized cassava root and has a very fine texture. How to Use Organic Cassava Flour When Baking. The best thing about Organic Cassava Flour is that this product can literally substitute all-purpose flour in a recipe without any additions. Unlike other types of gluten-free flours, this one is nearly identical to wheat in texture and chemical properties, so it acts the same when you add it to the dough. The only small difference is that it absorbs water a bit better. That’s why you should first have a few test runs with your baking recipes. The similarities between wheat and cassava flour mean that the baked goods will have a nearly identical texture as well. This won’t be the case if you use any other type of gluten-free flour as none other can fluff up the dough right. Organic Cassava Flour Vs/ Tapioca: Are They the Same? Do not mistake cassava flour for tapioca because despite coming from the same plant, these are two distinctly different products. Organic Cassava Flour is exactly that, it’s a flour made from whole cassava root. This means that it contains the fiber and other nutrients from the original plant. Tapioca, however, is starch derived from cassava root. As it’s starch only, it has no taste, very few nutrients, and its texture and chemical properties aren’t the same.

description:
Yam flour is powdered dried yam tuber widely used in food preparation. Typically white, the flour is commonly used in African dishes, such as Amala. It may be used in many other recipes if desired as well.

Yam Flour is a good choice for gluten-free recipes. Use of this flour is known to create lighter, fluffier products as well. High in carbohydrates, the food also contains some fat and protein. A cholesterol-free ingredient, the flour also contains a small amount of sodium and sugar.

Traditional Nigeria Amala is prepared with just yam flour and water. The flour is boiled until a dough is formed. The dough is then simmered in a small amount of water and kneaded before being served with a type of stew, such as one made from traditional vegetables and meats or fish.

Some people also utilize yam flour as a cheap base for dog treats or pet food. Animals with known wheat allergies may be fed with foods, such as dog cookies or biscuits, made with this type or other wheat-free flours. It's use is primarily popular in home-made pet treats.

Tasty cookies may be prepared with yam flour as well. The cookies may be prepared as any other sugar cookies, though milk is sometimes added to the recipe to prevent the flour from making the dough too dry.

If you want to make soft and delicious pastries, you definitely should use pastry flour. White Wheat Pastry Flour from Food To Live is made by stone-grinding soft wheat. This particular type of flour has a lower gluten content because it has less protein.

By the way, Did you know that protein creates a sticky substance we call gluten when flour mixes with water?

Furthermore, gluten is the element that affects the yeast in the dough. Its chemical love affair makes the yeast rise and stretch.

All-purpose flour has a higher gluten content. Therefore, it’s the right choice for bread and other recipes where the dough needs to rise.

Wheat Pastry Flour works much better for non-rising recipes; it gives your baked goods the delightfully soft and flaky texture by default.


When to Use Soft Wheat Pastry Flour

Sifted Wheat Flour is best used for pie crusts, homemade pasta, cookies, and croissants. You can also use it to make delicious blueberry muffins and cranberry scones. The idea is to use this type of flour when you want the pastries to be soft and fluffy in texture.

description:
What Is Organic Guar Gum?

Organic guar gum is a product made from the seeds of the guar plant. This substance has exceptional properties as a thickener and stabilizer. Therefore, it’s used in a variety of industries, but mostly in food production.

The vast majority of processed foods contain guar gum in some form and you can use it at home to make some treats. Organic Guar Gum from Food To Live is 100% free from any contaminants and safe for you and your family to enjoy.


How Is Guar Gum Produced?

The process of organic guar gum production is rather straightforward. Guar plant beans are harvested, dehusked, milled, and screened. Organic guar gum powder is the final product. Main producers of guar gum are India, Pakistan, Australia, and the US.

Organic guar gum price is fairly low compared to the cost of some other vegan food thickeners. Its production is cheap and the demand for this substance is huge as aside from food production, it’s used in hydraulic fracturing. The latter is a method of natural gas and oil extraction that gains popularity today.


Organic Guar Gum: Benefits and Side Effects

Organic guar gum isn’t a superfood and thus doesn’t offer any specific health benefits. You’ll only need to use less than a teaspoon of the product in most recipes. Therefore, organic guar gum nutrition value doesn’t really matter.

However, you’ll definitely get a tiny boost of fiber from it as guar gum contains huge amounts of it. When consumed in reasonable amounts, organic guar gum has no side-effects. This is why it’s an approved food ingredient.

However, eating too much guar gum might cause indigestion and other digestive issues, because this product is high in fiber.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most Great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is Certified Organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

Preparing the dough is an easy process:

description:
What Is Organic Guar Gum?

Organic guar gum is a product made from the seeds of the guar plant. This substance has exceptional properties as a thickener and stabilizer. Therefore, it’s used in a variety of industries, but mostly in food production.

The vast majority of processed foods contain guar gum in some form and you can use it at home to make some treats. Organic Guar Gum from Food To Live is 100% free from any contaminants and safe for you and your family to enjoy.


How Is Guar Gum Produced?

The process of organic guar gum production is rather straightforward. Guar plant beans are harvested, dehusked, milled, and screened. Organic guar gum powder is the final product. Main producers of guar gum are India, Pakistan, Australia, and the US.

Organic guar gum price is fairly low compared to the cost of some other vegan food thickeners. Its production is cheap and the demand for this substance is huge as aside from food production, it’s used in hydraulic fracturing. The latter is a method of natural gas and oil extraction that gains popularity today.


Organic Guar Gum: Benefits and Side Effects

Organic guar gum isn’t a superfood and thus doesn’t offer any specific health benefits. You’ll only need to use less than a teaspoon of the product in most recipes. Therefore, organic guar gum nutrition value doesn’t really matter.

However, you’ll definitely get a tiny boost of fiber from it as guar gum contains huge amounts of it. When consumed in reasonable amounts, organic guar gum has no side-effects. This is why it’s an approved food ingredient.

However, eating too much guar gum might cause indigestion and other digestive issues, because this product is high in fiber.

description:
What is Cassava?

Also known as yuca, cassava is a delicious root vegetable that becomes the perfect alternative for wheat when dried and ground using Otto’s proprietary preparation. This multi-purpose flour is naturally grain and gluten-free and perfect for Paleo lifestyles. Otto's Cassava Flour is a single-ingredient flour (no gums, fillers, or nasty additives) with the taste and texture of wheat! This easy-to-use flour subs 1:1 by weight (120g of Otto's per cup of all-purpose flour) or simply decrease by 25% if your recipe calls for cups and not grams.

What makes Cassava Flour different?

Other cassava flours begin as yuca that has been peeled by hand and fermented in the sun – this fermentation adds a considerably sour flavor and smell to the flour. Moreover, sun drying is impossible to regulate and leads to varying levels of humidity, creating mold. The smell and taste of these sun-dried cassava flours is often described as "sour," "fermented," or "musty."

Importance of cassava in the world

Cassava is the most important tropical root crop. Its starchy roots are a major source of dietary energy for more than 500 million people. ... Cassava can be stored in the ground for several seasons, thereby serving as a reserve food when other crops fail.

description:
You can easily make your baked goods more nutritious and delicious by adding some Barley Flour. Whole-Grain Barley Flour provides you with all the benefits of this incredible grain. It also contains some gluten. Therefore, you can use this flour on its own and not only in mixes since gluten helps the dough rise.

Food To Live Barley Flour is finely ground. It’s made from hulled barley using stone-grinding to minimize the loss of nutrients. By default, barley flour contains almost three times as much fiber as wheat flour.

Barley is also more nutritious than wheat. Therefore, this flour contains more essential minerals (iron and zinc) and B vitamins. The taste of whole-grain barley flour is also different. Whereas white wheat flour is almost tasteless, barley flour is mildly sweet and nutty. Therefore, by using it in a recipe, you enhance its taste even without any additional flavorings.


Finely Ground Barley Flour Uses and Storage Guide

Barley Flour contains some gluten, but only a little of it. Gluten is the ingredient that makes yeast rise and stretch. So this flour is best used in recipes where you don’t need the dough to rise.

For example, it’s the right choice for muffins, cookies, and flatbreads. You can also use it to make delicious and nutritious pancakes for breakfast.

If you want to add the benefits of barley to your bread or even pie crust, you can mix whole-grain barley flour with all-purpose flour.

Barley flour stores for about four months and needs to stay in a cool and dry place. Always keep it in a sealed airtight container. Double-check the seal after every use.

If you want to extend the shelf life of the flour, keep it in the freezer. But make sure that the container you use is 100% airtight. Otherwise, the flour will soak up moisture from the air.

description:
A Traditional Central American Corn Flour

 

Make your own tamales and tortillas at home! It’s fun and easy with authentic corn masa harina, a flavorful stone ground cornmeal that’s been precooked with limewater to make the dough pliable. Masa is also wonderful in recipes that call for cornmeal. 

Masa harina is a traditional Central American corn flour dried and treated by soaking and cooking the mature (hard) grain in a diluted solution of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or wood ash, a process termed nixtamalization. Soaking the corn loosens the hulls away from the kernels and softens the corn, while making it easier to digest and absorb the nutrients.

This process produces hominy, which is stone ground into masa. It is an excellent source of fiber, corn flour contains about 7.3 grams of fiber per 100 grams serving and helps to reduce constipation. It keeps you fuller longer for weight loss benefits.

It is the time-honored Central American and Mexican breakfast staple and is used in tortillas, corn chips, taco shells, tamales, and other traditional Mexican cuisine. It is the best way to elevate recipes for tacos, tamales, empanadas, and scores of authentic Mexican dishes. Make your family’s traditional recipes or create your own delicious  dishes!

description:
Delicious arepas can now be your specialty! Harina P.A.N. is one of the most popular brands of corn flour. Versatile and perfect for a wide range of
dishes such as arepas, empanadas, cornbread, bollos, hallacas, pupusas, tamales to mention just a few.

P.A.N. pre-cooked corn meal is a unique product made out of pure corn. Gluten-free and does not contain any preservatives, artificial colors or flavorings.
The production process is chemical free. Just by adding water, P.A.N. makes instant corn dough, creating a variety of delicious and easy corn based dishes
that can be adapted to different tastes and customs.

How to Prepare the Dough
Preparing the dough is an easy process:
– Pour 2 ½ cups of water into a container.
– Add salt and gradually mix in 2 ½ cups of corn meal.
– Briefly knead the mixture until a smooth dough is formed and then let it rest for 3 minutes.

How to Prepare Arepas
Separate dough in 10 pieces. Take one portion in your hands and shape it into a ball, then press it with your palms to form a large patty shape of about 10 cm
or 3 ½ inches in diameter. Place onto a griddle or frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes on each side, or until brown on both sides, and serve hot.
Open the arepa and fill it with cheese, ham, eggs, salad or anything else you might put in a sandwich.

About us

The product was intended to bear a name that represented all that an arepa meant, which is that it was to be the "Venezuelan bread" or "pan" in Spanish.
It was thus that it came be called P.A.N., acronym for Productos Alimenticios Nacionales.

On December 10, 1960 P.A.N. was launched and achieved great success, from a complete satisfaction of the Venezuelan consumer.

Today, P.A.N. is found in more than 60 countries, bringing the delicious flavor of corn to consumers in an easy and practical way to prepare their favorite
corn based recipes.

¡Las deliciosas arepas ahora pueden ser su especialidad! Harina P.A.N. es una de las marcas más populares de harina de maíz. Versátil y perfecto para una amplia gama de
platos como arepas, empanadas, pan de maíz, bollos, hallacas, pupusas, tamales por mencionar solo algunos.

P.A.N. harina de maíz precocida es un producto único hecho de maíz puro. Sin gluten y no contiene conservantes, colores artificiales ni saborizantes.
El proceso de producción es libre de químicos. Sólo agregando agua, P.A.N. hace masa de maíz instantánea, creando una variedad de deliciosos y fáciles platos a base de maíz
que se pueden adaptar a diferentes gustos y costumbres.

Cómo preparar la masa
Preparar la masa es un proceso fácil:
– Vierta 2 ½ tazas de agua en un recipiente.
– Agregue sal y mezcle gradualmente en 2 ½ tazas de harina de maíz.
– Amasar brevemente la mezcla hasta que se forme una masa suave y luego dejar reposar durante 3 minutos.

Cómo preparar Arepas
Separe la masa en 10 piezas. Tome una porción en sus manos y formaela en una bola, luego presione con las palmas para formar una gran forma de empanada de unos 3.9 in
o 3 ½ pulgadas de diámetro. Coloque en una plancha o sartén a fuego medio durante 5 minutos a cada lado, o hasta que se doren en ambos lados, y sirva caliente.
Abre la arepa y llénala con queso, jamón, huevos, ensalada o cualquier otra cosa que puedas poner en un sándwich.

recetas basadas en maíz.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers And pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Consuming organic foods promotes the health of individuals and the land on which it was grown. In supporting organic agriculture we promote the cycle of a healthy environment which includes the lives of microorganisms, plants, and humans. Most great River flour is stone-ground. We believe the natural granite millstones contribute to the quality, taste and nutritional integrity of whole grain flour. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor. The cooler Temperatures that occur during milling with stones allows important enzyme activity to continue. Protein levels are also be maintained. Our stone-ground flours are milled to order, to retain the nutritional value of the flour. Great River is certified organic by Quality Assurance International and Kosher Approved. Obtaining our certification requires a yearly inspection of our milling facility and records to insure that our products meet industry standards.

description:
If you want to make soft and delicious pastries, you definitely should use pastry flour. White Wheat Pastry Flour from Food To Live is made by stone-grinding soft wheat. This particular type of flour has a lower gluten content because it has less protein.

By the way, Did you know that protein creates a sticky substance we call gluten when flour mixes with water?

Furthermore, gluten is the element that affects the yeast in the dough. Its chemical love affair makes the yeast rise and stretch.

All-purpose flour has a higher gluten content. Therefore, it’s the right choice for bread and other recipes where the dough needs to rise.

Wheat Pastry Flour works much better for non-rising recipes; it gives your baked goods the delightfully soft and flaky texture by default.


When to Use Soft Wheat Pastry Flour

Sifted Wheat Flour is best used for pie crusts, homemade pasta, cookies, and croissants. You can also use it to make delicious blueberry muffins and cranberry scones. The idea is to use this type of flour when you want the pastries to be soft and fluffy in texture.

Note that soft wheat flour is rather tasteless. Therefore, it’s convenient that it can be used in almost any recipe. We find it works amazingly to make the batter for fried dishes.

description: With Organic Cassava Flour you can enjoy delicious cakes, buns, and other goodies with soft and fluffy texture even if you are gluten-intolerant. It’s made from dried and pulverized cassava root and has a very fine texture. How to Use Organic Cassava Flour When Baking. The best thing about Organic Cassava Flour is that this product can literally substitute all-purpose flour in a recipe without any additions. Unlike other types of gluten-free flours, this one is nearly identical to wheat in texture and chemical properties, so it acts the same when you add it to the dough. Do not mistake cassava flour for tapioca because despite coming from the same plant, these are two distinctly different products. Organic Cassava Flour is exactly that, it’s a flour made from whole cassava root. This means that it contains the fiber and other nutrients from the original plant. Tapioca, however, is starch derived from cassava root. As it’s starch only, it has no taste, very few nutrients, and its texture and chemical properties aren’t the same.

description: White Rice flour is a form of flour made from finely milled rice. It is distinct from rice starch, which is usually produced by steeping rice in lye. Rice flour is a common substitute for wheat flour. It is also used as a thickening agent in recipes that are refrigerated or frozen since it inhibits liquid separation. A staple in India, Japan, Southeast Asia and Thailand, rice flour is mainly used for making noodles, desserts and sweets. It is also an excellent thickener for sauces, custards and gravies. Potato flour is starch extracted from potatoes. The cells of the root tubers of the potato plant contain leucoplasts (starch grains). To extract the starch, the potatoes are crushed, and the starch grains are released from the destroyed cells. The starch is then washed out and dried to powder. Potato Flour attracts and holds water, producing moist yeast bread with a good shelf life. A teaspoon or so added to your baked goods lends a moist crumb, Tapioca flour is made from the crushed pulp of the cassava root (pictured below), a woody shrub native to South America and the Caribbean. Tapioca flour is a very fine, white powder that works well in gluten free baking. It can replace cornstarch as a thickener for pies, gravies, pudding, dough and sauces and aids in creating a crisp crust and chewy.

description:
Plantain flour is made by drying green, unripe plantains and grinding them to flour. Plantain flour is a healthier substitute for wheat flour and the all-purpose flour because it doesn't contain gluten which is the main protein found in wheat and barley.

►Garbanzo also known as Chickpeas are versatile legumes with a mild, nutty taste, and chickpea flour is typically made from a variety called Bengal grams. Garbanzo flour is packed with fiber, as chickpeas themselves are naturally high in this nutrient.

►Cassava flour comes from ground cassava root. It's fine and powdery and tends to create dust clouds if you don't handle it carefully. The taste is slightly nutty and earthy, though it can be easily used as a swap for all-purpose flour in gluten-free baking.

►Teff flour has traditionally been used to make injera, a fermented, sourdough-like Ethiopian bread. It's now also used for other foods like pancakes, cereals, breads and snacks. It can be substituted for 25–50% of wheat or all-purpose flour.

►Quinoa flour is made by grinding quinoa seeds to a fine consistency. It looks and feels like all-purpose wheat flour and is easily adapted to a broad range of baking recipes, from desserts to muffins to breads.

Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. description:
Who is Freekeh Foods?
When a seed is planted in the ground it grows from the roots down. It is with that much intention that we get connected to our ancient roots and bring protein rich grains from farm land to table. At Freekeh Foods, we cultivate a workplace culture that promotes ownership; we are family, employee, farmer, and processor owned.
What is Freekeh?
Freekeh is an ancient grain rooted in the Middle Eastern tradition of roasting young green wheat. The roasted grain has a nutty flavor and chewy texture that provider innovative meal options that are in demand.
Where is Freekeh Grown?
Customers want transparency on where their food comes from. Our company, Freekeh Foods, is the only company to grow and process Freekeh in the United States in 100% solar powered facility.
Why Freekeh?
Freekeh has a chewy texture and a nutty flavor that resonates with the plant-based foodie because Freekeh is a nutrient dense ancient grain. Freekeh is a good source of protein and fiber making it more nutritious than brown rice, bulgur, and similar grains.
When to Use Freekeh?
Freekeh is a versatile super grain that cooks perfectly in soups, pilafs, salads, stir-fries and stews, or can be stone ground into flour for baking purposes. Whether you are looking for plant-based vegetarian or vegan option, or to feature a unique grain in your culinary masterpieces; Freekeh is the smart choice.
How is Freekeh Cooked and Enjoyed?
Freekeh cooks like rice. Freekeh has a chewy texture that holds its tooth, even after a couple days in the refrigerator – it will not congeal like rice or quinoa when stored after cooking.
Freekeh is available in two varieties: cracked or whole.
Cracked Freekeh: Cracked to reduce cooking time Texture of bulgur with a nutty flavor and chewy texture Endless possibilities: breakfast cereal, cold salads, a side to your favorite protein, served as a vegan or vegetarian dinner.

description:
Rye is a family of wheat. Whole-grain rye flour contains the highest amount of bran. Therefore it's rich in proteins, vitamins, potassium, iron, and magnesium. Rye flour is popularly used in diets for people with diabetes since the rye's carbohydrates are brake down gradually and, therefore, prevent blood glucose levels from rising quickly. Rye contains many proteins and amino acids, so even athletes can benefit from it in their diet.
How does it taste and how can you use it

Rye flour possesses a unique taste and color. The taste is slightly bitter and nutty, which is surprising for those who like wheat bread.
Another quality of rye flour is its ability to become brown when baked. That is why the crumb of rye bread is always dark.
For a long time, whole rye flour was only for industrial baking of bread. However, nowadays, it is becoming more common, and the number of recipes with rye flour continuously grows. You can make cookies, pancakes, pies, tortillas, and other goodies from it. Different mixing proportions - different properties of your bread
Because bread flour possesses different characteristics than wheat flour, it is rarely used as a substitute. Instead, bakers use it to make a flour mix. Here are some examples of bread with the use of different proportions of rye and wheat flours:
The bread that has up to 40% rye flour, commonly referred to as "rye bread." Rye flour is in a reasonably large proportion here; therefore, there is a distinct rye flavor.
Bread with more than 50% rye flour is entirely different. All the unique characteristics of rye and wheat's chemical differences become more important as the proportion of rye in the dough increases. description:
Make your baked goods more delicious and nutritious by adding some Organic Spelt Flour to your recipes. This flour is stone-ground to minimize the loss of nutrients. It's naturally rich in fiber and plant protein, as well as essential minerals. Adding some whole spelt flour to your baked goods will ensure that you are getting some precious iron and zinc every mouthful.

Spelt is an ancient grain and a type of wheat. Therefore, Organic Spelt Wheat Flour isn't gluten-free. However, because of its lighter texture and lower content of gluten, this flour can be an excellent whole wheat alternative. It's safe for people who want to reduce their intake of gluten for dietary reasons.

Stone-ground organic spelt flour is similar to wheat by texture, but the grain itself is much more flavorful. It has a rich nutty and mildly-sweet flavor, without any bitterness of whole wheat.


How to Bake with Organic Spelt Flour

In essence, you can use organic white spelt flour in any recipe that requires wheat flour. It's best to replace about half of the flour in a recipe with spelt flour. It will allow you to see how it works in every recipe, and you can adjust your proportions in the future.

It's important to note that whole wheat spelt flour soaks up less liquid than wheat flour. Therefore, you'll need to cut down the number of liquid ingredients by a little bit. However, you can also add a bit more flour. It is necessary to prevent the dough from being too sticky.

Store your organic stone-ground spelt flour in an airtight container someplace cool and dark. In a pantry or a cupboard, it will last for six months. It will store in the fridge for a year so go ahead and buy Organic Spelt Flour bulk.

Azure Standard’s Unifine flour is milled at the Azure Farm Mill in Dufur, Ore., one of only a few such mills in the world, and family owned. The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. With this unique, one-step milling process the entire bran, germ and endosperm of the grain are retained, resulting in superior nutritious flour, and the oil molecules are left intact resulting in a longer shelf life. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

Who is Freekeh Foods?
When a seed is planted in the ground it grows from the roots down. It is with that much intention that we get connected to our ancient roots and bring protein rich grains from farm land to table. At Freekeh Foods, we cultivate a workplace culture that promotes ownership; we are family, employee, farmer, and processor owned.
What is Freekeh?
Freekeh is an ancient grain rooted in the Middle Eastern tradition of roasting young green wheat. The roasted grain has a nutty flavor and chewy texture that provider innovative meal options that are in demand.
Where is Freekeh Grown?
Customers want transparency on where their food comes from. Our company, Freekeh Foods, is the only company to grow and process Freekeh in the United States in 100% solar powered facility.
Why Freekeh?
Freekeh has a chewy texture and a nutty flavor that resonates with the plant-based foodie because Freekeh is a nutrient dense ancient grain. Freekeh is a good source of protein and fiber making it more nutritious than brown rice, bulgur, and similar grains.
When to Use Freekeh?
Freekeh is a versatile super grain that cooks perfectly in soups, pilafs, salads, stir-fries and stews, or can be stone ground into flour for baking purposes. Whether you are looking for plant-based vegetarian or vegan option, or to feature a unique grain in your culinary masterpieces; Freekeh is the smart choice.
How is Freekeh Cooked and Enjoyed?
Freekeh cooks like rice. Freekeh has a chewy texture that holds its tooth, even after a couple days in the refrigerator – it will not congeal like rice or quinoa when stored after cooking.
Freekeh is available in two varieties: cracked or whole.
Cracked Freekeh: Cracked to reduce cooking time Texture of bulgur with a nutty flavor and chewy texture Endless possibilities: breakfast cereal, cold salads, a side to your favorite protein, served as a vegan or vegetarian dinner.

The name “Unifine” comes from the milling process itself, where it takes just one step (uni) to produce a very fine, uniform consistency, while also preserving the natural nutrients of the grain. With Unifine Milling, the grain enters a high speed rotor with a single-pass impact system that instantly pulverizes the kernels with little heat involved, bursting into fine flour at a cool temperature. Whole grain Unifine Flours require the baker to use significantly more water than commercial white flours or other milled brands. With germ and bran intact, there should be less mixing or kneading, and longer time allowed for fermentation and rising. Baking with organic whole grain flours may take some practice and experimentation, but the resulting nutrition and superior taste are worth it.

description: Great River Organic Milling is located on the upper Mississippi River, in the heart of what is called the Hiawatha Valley. The natural beauty of the area is a constant reminder of the importance of our commitment to organic agriculture. Organic, or sustainable agriculture is more than the avoidance of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. An organic farm strives to protect our environment by building and maintaining healthy soil which, in turn, improves water and air quality. It has been shown that grain and other food crops grown in a healthy soil, resist pests and diseases better than conventionally grown crops and also contain more vital nutrients important to humans. Grain flowing into the stones becomes very thin, flat flakes which integrates all parts of the wheat immediately into the flour, allowing the flour to have more flavor.
